text.p: Ticor Ltd said on Monday it would form a joint venture with DuPont Co on a joint venture to expand a joint venture expansion of Ticor's sodium cyanide plant in Gladstone, Queensland.

Under the joint venture agreement, Ticor's existing sodium cyanide maufacturing facilities will be expanded to 43,000 tonnes per annum, making it Australia's largest producer, Ticor said. The expanded plant will start up by early 1998.

DuPont will continue to be the exclusive marketer for the output of the plant. The joint venture is to be managed by a new jointly-owned management company which will draw upon the existing operational skills of Ticor Chemical's staff, it said.
John Foote, chairman of DuPont Australia and New Zealand, said expansion of this facility supported the growing Australian gold mining industry with locally produced sodium cyanide.
Increasing local manufacturing capacity would avoid the gap in the sodium cyanide market currently being met by imported product, Foote said.

This joint venture would give the joint venture the capacity to meet the growing needs of the local industry while also approaching export markets such as New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Fiji and the Philippines, he said.
"I'm pleased to see this substantial investment in Australia by our parent company. It represents a growing confidence in Australia as a strategic market for investment," Foote said.
